title: Investigating the adsorption mechanism of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) towards different adsorbents with FT-ICR-MS
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are found in almost every location around the globe: in soil, in rivers, in ground water and in the oceans. Their ubiquitous occurrence leads to a high risk of contamination for all lifeforms, including humans where they can cause serious health issues. Thus, techniques are required to remove PFAS from the environment. In this work, the adsorption behaviour of PFAS towards a weak anion exchanger (WAX), a strong anion exchanger (SAX) and activated carbon granulate (ACG) was investigated. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctance sulfonic acid (PFOS) were chosen as PFAS representatives and their retention properties were quantified by Fourier-Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) using Electrospray Ionization (ESI) in negative mode. The shortest adsorption time was found for WAX. Their adsorption behaviour with respect to pH was tested and showed the best performance under physiological conditions thereby demonstrating their suitability for environmental remediation. Concentration dependence was measured and fitted by the models of Henry, Freundlich, Langmuir and the Brunauer, Emmett and Teller (BET) adsorption isotherm: across the three chemically distinct sorbents, the BET model gave the closest match to the isotherm shape and was the statistically preferred or equivalent model for PFOS. The results can be interpreted as evidence for an adsorption process extending beyond a single monolayer. For PFOA the BET and Freundlich models were comparable, although contributions from surface heterogeneity or pore filling cannot be excluded. The breakthrough curves (BTC) resulting from Mini-Column Experiments (MCE) were investigated and evaluated using Thomas fitting and compared with results from previous work using cobaltocenium complexes. This showed comparable capacities for WAX and ACG, whereas for SAX no BTC was achieved. Thus, the investigated adsorbents demonstrate efficient capture of PFOA and PFOS and suggest that they could be utilised for environmental remediation.
